Title: Reducing the fear of falling among community-dwelling elderly adults through cognitive-behavioural strategies and intense Tai Chi exercise: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Huang, Yang & Liu
Comment: The reported F=4.09 is an omnibus three-group ANOVA and the post hoc result identifies only CB + Tai Chi versus control (3 > 1); no direct CB-versus-control significance statistic is reported, so no test statistic or p value is assigned to this row. FES is a confidence scale, so its mean must be sign-reversed before computing an SMD oriented so lower values mean less fear. The control arm is shared by two eligible comparisons; n=61 is retained because it is the paper's verbatim analyzed count, but the meta-analysis must split its effective sample size equally across the two comparisons.
Study Environment: Rural community; outcomes assessed in participants' homes
Topic of Content: Cognitive restructuring and behavioural management of fear of falling
Participant type: Community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older
Recruitment source: Residents of registered households in a rural community in Yi-Lan county, northeastern Taiwan
Outcome measurement: Fall Efficacy Scale total score; confidence in ten activities of daily living, with higher scores indicating greater confidence
additional_group_ns: CB + Tai Chi: n=56 at 2 months

Author: Barbara Resnick, Daria Luisi, and Amanda Vogel
Comment: The trial randomized senior-center clusters (6 intervention, 7 control), but the authors made no correction for clustering because site differences were not statistically significant. No ICC or cluster-adjusted fear-of-falling result is reported, so an effective sample-size adjustment cannot be performed from this paper alone. The per-arm Ns (64 and 39) are overall follow-up counts, not explicitly outcome-specific analyzed counts. Comment: The reported 0.61 is the ANCOVA-adjusted mean difference, whereas 7.79 and 7.45 are unadjusted observed post-intervention means. Title: Effects of a Multicomponent Cognitive Behavioral Group Intervention on Fear of Falling and Activity Avoidance in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Results of a Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Zijlstra et al.
Comment: The post-intervention means and SDs are crude, whereas M_diff is the baseline- and covariate-adjusted mixed-effects estimate. Final analyzed per-arm Ns for this continuous outcome were not explicitly reported, so group Ns and total analyzed N are left null; randomized Ns (260 control, 280 intervention) were not substituted. SE_diff was derived from the reported 95% CI as (-0.20 - (-2.81))/3.92 = 0.6658, and the treatment-coefficient test statistic was derived as -1.51/0.6658 = -2.27. Hedges' g was not computed because final analyzed per-arm Ns were unavailable. Title: Long-Term Effects of Three Multicomponent Exercise Interventions on Physical Performance and Fall-Related Psychological Outcomes in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Ellen Freiberger; Lothar Häberle; Waneen W. Spirduso; G. A. Rixt Zijlstra
Comment: The extracted group means and SDs are the paper's crude ABC scores. ABC is a confidence scale on which higher scores mean greater confidence/less fear; reverse the means' sign before computing the synthesis SMD so that lower values indicate less fear. The 6-month assessment is the earliest ABC measurement reported; the 16-week intervention had ended before this assessment, but it was not within approximately one month of intervention end. The adjusted mixed-effects mean difference (-5.23, 95% CI -11.25 to 0.78) is recorded in M_diff, while the requested SMD should be calculated from the crude post-intervention N, mean, and SD values. No exact P value was reported. SBG and FG were excluded as exercise-only arms.

Title: Effectiveness of a home-based cognitive behavioral program to manage concerns about falls in community-dwelling, frail older people: results of a randomized controlled trial
Author: Dorresteijn et al.
Comment: The adjusted mean difference and its confidence interval come from an intention-to-treat mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline score, stratification level of concerns about falls, age, gender, perceived general health, and prior falls. The reported 95% CI is one-sided with an infinite lower bound, so SE_diff was not derived. The p value is reported only as P < .001; 0.001 records the stated threshold rather than an exact p value. Group means, SDs, and analyzed Ns are the directly reported post-intervention values suitable for SMD calculation. FES-I already has the required direction (higher = more fear), so no sign reversal is needed.

Medium: Intervention delivered through home visits and telephone contacts; outcome collected by telephone interview

Topic of Content: Managing concerns about falls using cognitive restructuring, goal setting, action planning, motivational interviewing, safe behavior, and exposure in vivo
interaction_type: Individual nurse-facilitated home and telephone sessions
Participant type: Community-dwelling frail people aged 70 years or older with concerns about falls and related activity avoidance
